segments.text: This morning, I had one of those "I just can't be bothered" moments. And of course, it came back to bite me. I was getting ready, running a bit behind, and I saw the shirt I wanted to wear. It looked fine, kind of. You know that level of wrinkled where it's not terrible, but it's definitely not good. I stared at it for a solid 10 seconds, debating iron it or pretend it doesn't look that bad. And since I was already tired and honestly not in the mood to deal with an iron, I went with option two. I threw it on, smoothed it out with my hands, like that ever works, and headed out. I felt okay about it until I caught my reflection in a window. The shirt looked worse than I remembered, way worse. It had that fresh-out-of-the-dryer-but-actually-not-dry-yet kind of texture. Then, of course, I ran into someone I knew and the whole time we were talking, I couldn't focus because all I could think was, "Why didn't I just take the extra two minutes to iron this thing?" By the time I got where I was going, the regret was real. The shirt kept folding in weird places and every mirror I passed reminded me of the terrible decision I made this morning. It's funny, the one day I couldn't be bothered to iron my clothes was exactly the day I should've.
